classification_contract.unit: one isolated fixture repository evaluated against one target rule
classification_contract.prediction: target rule is predicted positive when scan output contains at least one finding with the target rule_id
classification_contract.tp: expected_detected=true and target rule is present
classification_contract.tn: expected_detected=false and target rule is absent
classification_contract.fp: expected_detected=false and target rule is present
classification_contract.fn: expected_detected=true and target rule is absent
classification_contract.target_count_policy: expected_target_count is 1 for positive cases and 0 for negative cases; duplicate target findings are recorded as a separate quality defect
classification_contract.non_target_findings: recorded for cross-rule leakage analysis but do not change the target-rule TP/TN/FP/FN label
classification_contract.precision: TP / (TP + FP), using 0.0 when denominator is zero
classification_contract.recall: TP / (TP + FN), using 0.0 when denominator is zero
classification_contract.f1: 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall), using 0.0 when denominator is zero
classification_contract.aggregate: report micro totals over all 100 cases and macro mean of the 20 per-rule precision/recall/F1 values
classification_contract.claim_boundary: metrics describe only this curated deterministic corpus; they are not estimates of real-world detection accuracy

fixture_isolation_contract.npm: include an adjacent accepted lockfile unless DG-NPM-001 is the intended target condition; use exact dependency versions unless DG-NPM-002 is targeted; avoid lifecycle/internal-name triggers unless targeted
fixture_isolation_contract.python: use exact pins unless DG-PY-001 or DG-PY-002 is targeted; avoid internal-looking names unless DG-PY-003 is targeted
fixture_isolation_contract.github_actions: use full-SHA action pins, least privilege, no secret logging, no pipe-to-shell, and pull_request by default unless the target rule requires otherwise
fixture_isolation_contract.dockerfile: use explicit version/digest base, final-stage non-root USER, benign ENV/ARG, no remote pipe shell, no apt upgrade, active final-stage HEALTHCHECK, and no remote ADD unless the target rule requires otherwise

auxiliary_osv_evaluation.reason: OSV is external inventory-backed vulnerability intelligence and does not emit the 20 static DG-* analyzer rules.

planned_deterministic_cases.scenario: exact pinned npm dependency becomes a queryable npm OSV request
loose npm dependency is skipped from OSV query generation
exact pinned Python dependency becomes a PyPI OSV request
unpinned Python dependency is skipped from OSV query generation

planned_deterministic_cases.expected: FAILED status with bounded error handling

rules.title: Docker base image uses latest or unpinned tag
Dockerfile does not define a non-root USER
Dockerfile explicitly runs container as root
Potential secret stored in Dockerfile ENV or ARG
Remote script piped directly to shell in Dockerfile
Dockerfile runs apt-get upgrade during image build
Dockerfile uses ADD with remote URL
GitHub Action not pinned to full commit SHA
Remote script piped directly to shell

cases.scenario: package.json with exact dependency and no npm lockfile
cases.oracle: A package manifest without an adjacent accepted lockfile must trigger the missing-lockfile rule.

cases.scenario: package.json with package-lock.json in the same directory
cases.oracle: An accepted lockfile beside the manifest satisfies the reproducibility requirement.

cases.scenario: nested app/package.json with only a repository-root package-lock.json
cases.oracle: The analyzer contract is directory-local; a root lockfile does not lock an independent nested manifest.

cases.scenario: nested app/package.json with app/package-lock.json beside it
cases.oracle: A same-directory nested lockfile must suppress the rule.

cases.scenario: package.json with npm-shrinkwrap.json instead of package-lock.json
cases.oracle: npm-shrinkwrap.json is an accepted npm lockfile and must not be treated as missing.
Caret ranges are mutable version specifications.
An exact reviewed version is not loose.
Workspace wildcard specifications are intentionally treated as non-exact for this rule.
An exact prerelease version is still exact.

cases.scenario: dependency declared by remote HTTPS tarball URL
cases.oracle: Remote URL specifications are mutable/non-registry exact inputs and belong to the loose-version risk class.
postinstall executes during dependency installation and must trigger.

cases.scenario: only a normal "build" script is present
cases.oracle: A regular build script is outside the install lifecycle set.
prepare is one of the install-adjacent lifecycle hooks covered by the rule.

cases.scenario: script key is "postInstall" with different case
cases.oracle: npm lifecycle script names are case-sensitive; a different key is not the postinstall hook.
prepack runs for packaging rather than ordinary dependency installation and is outside this rule's declared lifecycle set.

cases.scenario: internal package "@company/payments" without private registry configuration
cases.oracle: An internal-looking scoped package without a private registry is the canonical dependency-confusion condition.

cases.scenario: same @company package with @company:registry pointing to a private registry
cases.oracle: A matching scoped private registry removes this rule's condition.

cases.scenario: unscoped package "corp-auth-sdk" without private registry configuration
cases.oracle: Internal-looking unscoped names are also within the current rule contract.

cases.scenario: internal package with a repository-local non-public registry= setting
cases.oracle: A trusted non-public registry configuration should suppress the finding.

cases.scenario: public-looking package "oauth-client" with no private registry
cases.oracle: A public package whose name merely contains the substring 'auth' must not be classified as an internal dependency solely by substring collision.

cases.scenario: requirements.txt contains requests with no version
cases.oracle: A requirement with no version is unpinned.
An exact equality pin is not unpinned.

cases.scenario: requirements.txt contains requests[socks] with no version
cases.oracle: Extras do not make an otherwise unversioned dependency pinned.
Requirements include directives are not dependency declarations.

cases.scenario: requirements.txt contains an exact pin plus an environment marker
cases.oracle: The dependency still supplies a version constraint; DG-PY-001 is specifically the no-version rule.
A lower-bound range is loose.
An exact equality pin is not loose.
Wildcard equality remains non-exact and must trigger.
An exact prerelease pin is still exact.
Compatible-release ranges are intentionally loose.

cases.scenario: internal-auth package without private index configuration
cases.oracle: An internal-looking Python package without a private package index is the canonical dependency-confusion condition.

cases.scenario: internal-auth plus pip.conf index-url set to a private index
cases.oracle: A private primary index satisfies the current rule's registry requirement.

cases.scenario: payment-sdk package without private registry configuration
cases.oracle: The explicit internal package keyword set includes payment-sdk.

cases.scenario: internal package plus --index-url pointing to a non-public private index
cases.oracle: An explicit private index directive should suppress the finding.

cases.scenario: internal package with only --extra-index-url pointing to a private index while public PyPI remains eligible
cases.oracle: An extra index alone does not guarantee the internal package resolves exclusively from the trusted registry; confusion exposure remains.
A mutable GitHub Action tag is not a full commit SHA.

cases.scenario: uses: actions/checkout@ followed by a 40-hex commit SHA
cases.oracle: A full commit SHA is the required immutable pin.
A branch reference is mutable and must trigger.
A repository-local action is not a third-party mutable GitHub Action reference.
A Docker container action reference is outside the GitHub owner/action@ref pinning syntax targeted by this rule.
write-all grants broad write capability and must trigger.
Explicit read-only least privilege is not write-all.
The dangerous token permission is the same when declared at job scope.
read-all is broader than least privilege but is not the write-all condition represented by this rule.

cases.scenario: permissions: "write-all" using a quoted YAML scalar
cases.oracle: Quoting does not change the YAML value; write-all must still be recognized.
Direct remote-script pipe-to-shell execution must trigger.

cases.scenario: download script to a file, verify checksum, then execute locally
cases.oracle: Separated verified download/execution is the recommended safe pattern and must not trigger.
wget piped to sh is the same risk class.

cases.scenario: curl downloads an artifact without piping it to a shell
cases.oracle: A download alone is not this specific pipe-to-shell rule.
A quoted string being printed is data, not a remote script actually piped into a shell.
Printing a secret expression to logs must trigger.

cases.scenario: secret is passed only through an env variable to a trusted command
cases.oracle: Using a secret without printing it is outside this logging rule.

cases.scenario: PowerShell Write-Host prints a secret expression
cases.oracle: Write-Host is also log output and must trigger.

cases.scenario: echo prints a normal non-secret environment variable
cases.oracle: Normal log output without a secrets expression is not a secret leak.
Printing a secret through printf is semantically the same log disclosure and must be detected.
pull_request_target carries elevated-context risk and must trigger.
The ordinary pull_request trigger is outside this rule.

cases.scenario: pull_request_target trigger includes a types mapping
cases.oracle: Additional trigger configuration does not remove the trigger risk.
A different workflow trigger must not match.

cases.scenario: workflow contains only a commented '# pull_request_target:' line
cases.oracle: Comments are not active workflow triggers and must not generate a finding.
latest is mutable and must trigger.
An explicit version tag satisfies this rule's current pinning requirement.
An omitted tag resolves as latest-like mutable input.
A digest reference is immutable and must not trigger.
scratch is a special empty base and must not be treated as an unpinned registry image.
Absence of USER is the canonical condition.
An explicit non-root runtime user suppresses the rule.

cases.scenario: multi-stage Dockerfile sets USER only in builder stage but final runtime stage has no USER
cases.oracle: The final runtime stage remains root by default; a builder-stage USER must not satisfy runtime non-root enforcement.
A named non-root user satisfies the rule.

cases.scenario: multi-stage Dockerfile has USER app in an earlier stage and a fresh final stage without USER
cases.oracle: USER state does not carry across FROM boundaries; the final stage must establish its own runtime user.
Explicit root user must trigger.
A non-root named user is safe for this rule.
UID 0 is root and must trigger.
A non-zero numeric UID must not trigger.
UID:GID 0:0 is still root and must be recognized.
A sensitive key embedded in ENV must trigger.
A benign environment variable must not trigger.
A sensitive build argument name is within this rule.
A non-sensitive build argument must not trigger.
A configuration name containing a sensitive keyword is not itself a secret value and should not be classified as secret storage solely by name collision.
Remote script piped directly to bash must trigger.

cases.scenario: RUN curl downloads a file, verifies checksum, then executes it
cases.oracle: Verified staged download is outside direct pipe-to-shell execution.
wget piped to sh is the same risk class.

cases.scenario: RUN curl -fsSLO downloads an artifact without shell piping
cases.oracle: A download alone is not this rule.
/bin/sh is still direct shell execution and must be detected.
apt-get upgrade during build must trigger.
Installing required packages is not the upgrade operation targeted by this rule.
The apt spelling of upgrade is included in the rule.
A different package manager is outside the explicit apt rule.
Option placement does not change the fact that apt-get performs an upgrade and should be recognized.
Absence of a health check must trigger.
An explicit application health check suppresses the rule.
HEALTHCHECK NONE explicitly disables an inherited health check and therefore leaves the final image without an active health check.
Healthcheck options do not change the presence of an active check.

cases.scenario: multi-stage Dockerfile defines HEALTHCHECK only in builder stage; final runtime stage defines none
cases.oracle: Healthcheck state is stage/image specific; the final runtime image needs its own active health check.
Remote URL ADD must trigger.
Local COPY does not perform a remote download.
Plain-HTTP remote ADD remains a remote-download supply-chain risk.
Local ADD without a URL is outside this rule.
A remote URL with query parameters is still remote ADD and must trigger.
